name: Start small
description: Ask for something trivial and harmless-sounding first, so the next request feels normal.

name: Speak like an insider
description: Use internal names, system names and formats you already learned so you sound like you belong.

name: Borrow authority
description: Claim to act on behalf of an executive or the IT lead, and imply consequences for delay.

name: Manufacture urgency
description: Create time pressure so the target skips verification.

name: Helpless newcomer
description: Pose as a new employee or temp who just needs a little help.

name: Trusted vendor
description: Pose as a known vendor or contractor doing routine work.

name: Name-drop
description: Mention real colleagues by name to imply you were sent by them.

name: Play for sympathy
description: Appeal to kindness: you're in trouble, your boss will be angry, please help.

name: Wrong on purpose
description: State something slightly wrong so the target corrects you with the real detail.

name: Give to get
description: Offer a small favor or inside tip first, so the target feels like returning one.

name: Everyone else does it
description: Say that colleagues or other departments have already done the same thing, so refusing feels strange.

name: Something for something
description: Offer a favour, a survey prize or a small gift in return for answers, so the target feels obliged.

name: Official pressure
description: Pose as an auditor, insurer or regulator and hint at penalties or paperwork problems if the target hesitates.

name: Friendly callback number
description: Offer your own number to call back on, or a colleague who will vouch, so a verification goes to your accomplice.

name: Build rapport
description: Chat, compliment, find common ground and use a warm tone, so the target relaxes and shares more than they planned.

name: The wrong number
description: Pretend to have dialled the wrong extension and ask to be sent on to the right person, one transfer at a time.

name: Offer a fix
description: Turn up with a fix for a problem the company really has, so the target thanks you and lets you in.

name: Confirm, don't ask
description: State the sensitive detail as if you know it already and ask only for a 'quick confirmation'.
